clue.text: Top cop covers up weird tattoos

indicators.note: one piece wraps around the other, covering it up on both sides

parts.note: DS is a Detective Superintendent (or Sergeant), a senior police rank
rum is old slang for strange or odd

explanation.surface: A senior police officer hides some odd tattoos under his clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tattoos' here is the verb for beating out a rhythm, not the body art.
explanation.definitionFit: To tattoo is to beat a steady rhythm with the fingers, which is what someone who drums does.

clue.text: New arrival carefully selected — 'doubtful breeding', say British involved

indicators.note: the letter for British is caught up inside
doubtful breeding is breeding gone awry, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A baby chosen for its traits raises questions of dubious breeding, with Britain involved.
explanation.definitionFit: A designer baby is a child whose genes are chosen in advance, a newborn picked to specification.

clue.text: With no prospect of compensation, totally loveless marriage turned bitter

indicators.note: love is O in tennis, so totally loveless means every O removed

parts.note: a union is a marriage
soured means turned bitter

explanation.surface: A spouse in a sour, loveless marriage expects nothing from the divorce.
explanation.definitionFit: An uninsured person has no cover, so no payout follows a loss.

clue.text: Smart though not quiet — they're in the groove

indicators.note: though not means without, so these letters go

parts.note: stylish means smart
sh is the call for quiet

explanation.surface: Cool people in the groove may be smart without being quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the groove' sounds like hip slang; the groove is a record's.
explanation.definitionFit: A stylus is the needle of a record player that runs along the record's track.

clue.text: Incitement to treason by politicians ultimately? Correct — one charged

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of politicians

parts.note: to edit is to correct a text
an ion is an atom carrying an electric charge

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether politicians are ultimately guilty of incitement, and is told yes — one has been charged.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedition is speech or conduct stirring people to rebel against the state.

clue.text: Is topless, rich and amusing (duke kept back money for immoral purposes)

indicators.note: topless means the first letter is lost

parts.note: lush means rich or luxurious
fun means amusing

explanation.surface: Something topless, lavish and entertaining is going on, while a duke hides money for vice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kept back' places the duke's letter at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A slush fund is cash set aside for bribes or other illicit payments.

clue.text: Shot by nasty piece of work over drugs

indicators.note: over in a down clue means turned over, read backwards

parts.note: a sod is an unpleasant person
E is short for ecstasy, standing for drugs

explanation.surface: A villain shot someone over drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: A dose is a measured shot of medicine or drug.

clue.text: Woman doctor has to pull out — might this prevent misrepresentation?

indicators.note: the pull word sits outside the others

parts.note: to tug is to pull
Ruth is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman doctor has to withdraw, perhaps so nothing gets misrepresented.
explanation.definitionFit: A truth drug is a substance supposedly forcing a subject to answer honestly.

clue.text: Partly uprooted catnip, roses and stonecrop

indicators.note: in a down clue uprooted pulls the letters up, so they read upwards
partly means only part of these words is used

explanation.surface: Some catnip, roses and stonecrop have been pulled up in a garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Orpin, also orpine, is a succulent plant of the sedum family.

clue.text: Move to settle up Stormy's suit — that's about right

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go about, around, the letter for right
to settle the words is to sort them into a new order

explanation.surface: A lawyer moves to settle a lawsuit brought by someone called Stormy, and thinks the figure is about right.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls Stormy Daniels's lawsuits against Donald Trump.
explanation.definitionFit: Stir your stumps is a British idiom urging someone to hurry up and get going.

clue.text: In war one's hit easily going over the top? No

indicators.note: the words are rearranged loosely, easily, into the answer

explanation.surface: In war a soldier may easily be hit going over the top, so better not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going over the top' evokes trench warfare; here it means excess.
explanation.definitionFit: Within reason means moderately, without excess.

clue.text: Manipulate mind of blonde by talk

parts.note: gas is idle chatter, so to gas is to talk
light describes fair, pale-coloured hair

explanation.surface: A blonde woman is psychologically manipulated by what she is told.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface nods to the film Gaslight, in which Ingrid Bergman's character is made to doubt her own sanity.
explanation.definitionFit: To gaslight someone is to make them doubt their own perception of reality, a psychological manipulation.

clue.text: Outsiders removed from noisy party — language!

indicators.note: the first and last letters, the outsiders, are taken away

parts.note: a shindig is a lively, noisy party

explanation.surface: Gatecrashers are thrown out of a rowdy party, amid much swearing.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation mark makes 'language!' sound like a rebuke for swearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Hindi is the most widely spoken tongue of northern India.

clue.text: Writer's book not a lot of money

definitions.note: read as writer is, so the definition is the writer

parts.note: Ezra is a book of the Old Testament
a pound is a modest sum

explanation.surface: An author complains that the book earned very little.
explanation.definitionFit: Ezra Pound was an American modernist poet, author of the Cantos.

clue.text: Take fright over US politician's suggestions initially for Covid etc

indicators.note: the fright word stretches over the politician

parts.note: to panic is to take fright
DEM is short for Democrat

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter

explanation.surface: People panic about a US politician's suggestions for handling Covid.
explanation.definitionFit: Covid-19 was a worldwide outbreak of disease, one of a class of global epidemics.

clue.text: Cut up nurses worried that it's life-threatening

indicators.note: nurses means holds, so one goes inside the other
up in a down clue reads the letters upwards

parts.note: pared means cut or trimmed

indicators.note: something worried is agitated and churned about, so the letters of that are jumbled

explanation.surface: Nurses are cut up and anxious about something dangerous.
explanation.definitionFit: A death trap is a structure or vehicle so dangerous it may kill.

clue.text: Make break — not Bingham's first

indicators.note: not tells us to leave the following letter out

parts.note: a breach is a break, as in a wall

indicators.note: Bingham's first means the opening letter of that name

explanation.surface: It sounds like snooker: make a break, without Stuart Bingham going first.
explanation.walkthrough: Bingham can be snooker player Stuart Bingham or Lord Lucan (Richard John Bingham), who made his famous escape.
explanation.definitionFit: To reach a place is to make it, as in making the station in time.

clue.text: Robot (the writer's out for himself) on a Sky feature

indicators.note: out for means the first letter goes and is replaced by the second

parts.note: an android is a humanoid robot
the writer is I, the setter
the writer's himself is ME

explanation.surface: A robot is out, and the writer appears in his place on a Sky TV programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sky' looks like the broadcaster; it is the night sky.
explanation.definitionFit: Andromeda is a constellation and galaxy visible in the night sky.

clue.text: Parisian right about director — 24 didn't want him

indicators.note: the French word goes around the letter for director

parts.note: bien is French for well or right, so it is a Parisian's word

explanation.surface: A French right-winger shrugs about a film director, while the clue's cross-reference points to unhappy rioters.
explanation.walkthrough: 24 is CAPITOL RIOTERS, the mob who stormed the US Capitol in January 2021 to stop the election result being confirmed.
explanation.definitionFit: Joe Biden's election victory was what the January 2021 mob tried to overturn.

clue.text: Gerard's visit to mother-in-law lasted too long!

indicators.note: Gerard's short name goes into, visits, the dragon

parts.note: a dragon is a fierce, domineering woman, the stock joke mother-in-law
Ged is a pet form of the name Gerard

explanation.surface: A man's visit to his formidable mother-in-law went on for far too long.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'Gerard's visit to mother-in-law' sound like the subject of the sentence; it is wordplay, with the definition at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that dragged on continued tediously beyond its welcome.

clue.text: Fellow with empty pockets swapping sides

indicators.note: the letter for right is exchanged for the letter for left

parts.note: broke means having no money

explanation.surface: A penniless man keeps changing his political allegiance.
explanation.walkthrough: R and L stand for right and left, the two sides.
explanation.definitionFit: Bloke is informal British for a man or chap.

clue.text: Back-to-back in South Island location

indicators.note: back means the word to is reversed

parts.note: ago means back in time, as in years back

explanation.surface: Sounds like a place where things are arranged back-to-back.
explanation.definitionFit: Otago is a region of New Zealand's South Island.

clue.text: At a certain place accepting incitement to action in name of ex-president

indicators.note: the place word takes in, accepts, the other letters

parts.note: there means at that place
O, DO is a cry urging someone to act: oh, do!

explanation.surface: Somewhere a speech inciting action is delivered in a former president's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Theodore Roosevelt was the 26th US president, so it is the forename of a former leader.

clue.text: English tenor enthralled by sailor's instruments

indicators.note: enthralled by means held inside

parts.note: OS is an ordinary seaman, a sailor
Alfie Boe is an English tenor

explanation.surface: An English singer is captivated by a sailor's instruments.
explanation.walkthrough: Alfie Boe is an English tenor known for musicals such as Les Misérables.
explanation.definitionFit: Oboes are woodwind instruments played with a double reed.

clue.text: Cross closer to turn

indicators.note: to turn the word is to read it in reverse

parts.note: a door closes an opening, so it is a closer

explanation.surface: Someone angry turns closer.
explanation.definitionFit: A rood is a crucifix, especially one above a church screen.

clue.text: Licit operators in action? Not at all!

definitions.text: Licit operators in action? Not at all!

indicators.note: the letters are set in motion and rearranged

explanation.surface: Asks whether these are lawful people at work, and answers firmly no.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram makes the people of the answer, and the 'Not at all!' says they were anything but lawful.
explanation.definitionFit: The mob that stormed the US Capitol in January 2021 were acting illegally, the opposite of licit.

clue.text: Look spent and ruined

parts.note: lo is an old exclamation meaning look
used up means spent or exhausted

explanation.surface: Someone appears exhausted and wrecked.
explanation.definitionFit: Loused up is slang for spoilt or botched.

clue.text: Foul dictator has lost out

indicators.note: out tells us the letter is removed

parts.note: Stalin was the Soviet dictator
L is the abbreviation for lost in sports tables

explanation.surface: A wicked dictator has been defeated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foul' looks like an adjective describing the dictator; it is a verb, the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To foul something is to soil or pollute it, which is to stain it.
